faq: Which sales channels can you sync?
Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Amazon, eBay, Etsy and others where a sync app or API exists. We confirm your channels before starting and tell you any limits.
Do my products need matching SKUs?
Yes. Matching codes are how channels know that two listings are the same item. We clean up missing and duplicate SKUs as part of the work and keep a list of the changes.
Will sync apps cost me monthly?
Most do, and prices depend on product count. We pick the lowest cost option that does the job, and tell you the price before we install anything.
What if the counts still drift?
We include a guide to find the cause, such as manual edits or delays. At Premium level we also set up a daily check that points out mismatches.

desc:
Inventory sync across stores and channels keeps your stock counts the same wherever you sell. Ecom Swift LLC connects your store and marketplaces, matches products by SKU and tests with real sales, so a sale in one place updates all the others.

## What is inventory syncing?

Inventory syncing is the automatic updating of stock numbers between your store, your marketplaces and any warehouse or location that holds goods. When a unit sells in one channel, the count falls in every other channel, so no channel offers something you no longer have.

Sync is done with an app or with your platform's own multichannel tools. Both rely on one thing: each product must be recognized as the same item in every place, which is why SKUs matter.

## Why stock counts drift and what it costs

Counts drift when sales happen faster than people update spreadsheets, or when two systems handle the same product under different names. The result is overselling. A customer pays for something you cannot ship, and you must cancel, apologize and refund.

Marketplaces can be strict about cancellations, which makes the problem worse. Even on your own store, a cancelled order damages trust. Syncing reduces the number of those moments by making the stock number a single shared fact.

## How accurate stock improves operations

Correct counts help in three places. Shoppers see real availability, so they do not order out-of-stock goods. Your team packs from reliable numbers, so fewer pick errors happen. You reorder at the right time, because low stock alerts reflect all channels together, not only one.

A safety buffer adds a further layer. Holding back a few units per channel gives you room for delays between a sale and the sync, so fast-moving items do not oversell during a busy moment.

## What a dependable sync setup includes

- A sync method chosen to match your channels and product volume.
- Products matched across channels by SKU.
- Clean-up of duplicate, missing or inconsistent SKUs.
- Rules for variants, bundles and kits.
- A safety stock buffer for each channel.
- Stock rules for more than one location or warehouse.
- Low stock alerts sent to the right person.
- A regular check that flags mismatched counts.
- Test sales that confirm each update.
- A short guide for fixing a count that looks wrong.

## What we do

We start by listing every place stock lives and every channel that sells it. We audit your SKUs, fix duplicates and make sure each product and variant has one identifier. Then we set up the sync in your own accounts, choosing a trusted sync app or the platform's built-in tools according to what fits your channels.

Next we write the rules: how a bundle takes stock from its parts, how much buffer each channel keeps and what happens at zero. We run test sales across channels and watch each count change, correcting any step that fails. At handover you receive a short guide explaining how the sync works and what to do if a number looks off.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of channels and products, and in whether we add variant rules, several locations and a regular mismatch check. Sync apps often have their own monthly fee, paid directly to the app maker, and we tell you before you commit.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give every product and variant one unique SKU.
- Choose one place as the source of truth for counts.
- Keep a small buffer on fast sellers.
- Check counts after any big sale or receipt of stock.
- Record manual changes with a reason.

**Avoid:**
- Editing stock in two places at once.
- Reusing a SKU for a different product.
- Syncing before duplicates are cleaned.
- Trusting the sync without a test sale.
- Ignoring low stock alerts.

## Who this is for

This suits a seller who has just added a marketplace and noticed that numbers no longer agree. It suits a store with a warehouse and a retail location that share stock. It also suits an owner who is tired of cancelling orders after an oversell.

## What we need from you

Send us a list of your channels, the tools you use and an export of your products with SKUs if you have one. Add us as a collaborator or staff user in each account where we need to work. We do not ask for passwords. We reply with a short plan, then tell you what we found in your SKUs.
